title: People: clause order
summary: Use the English meaning and Swedish context to choose or type the missing word or phrase.

s01.sentenceGloss: I know a woman who speaks five languages.

s02.sentenceGloss: She smiles because she is happy.

s03.sentenceGloss: I know that she does not work on Sundays.
s03.note: In the att clause, inte precedes arbetar.

s04.sentenceGloss: He says that he has never been to Norway.
s04.note: Aldrig precedes har in the subordinate clause.

s05.sentenceGloss: Because it is raining, we are at home.
s05.note: The initial subordinate clause is followed by the finite verb är.

s06.sentenceGloss: She may perhaps come tomorrow, but she is not sure.

s07.sentenceGloss: I think that he is at home.
s07.note: Att introduces the statement being believed.

s08.sentenceGloss: We have dinner when everyone has come home.
